title_options: You Use 40 kg Of This Molecule Every Day ⚡

share.myth: Your body stores the energy it needs, like a battery that slowly runs down.
share.truth: A resting person uses about 40 kg of ATP a day but holds only about 100 g at any moment, so every ATP molecule is rebuilt hundreds of times a day (Tymoczko, Berg & Stryer, Biochemistry: A Short Course).
share.line: You hold only about a hundred grams of ATP, yet you burn through about forty kilograms of it every day.

facts: Tymoczko, Berg & Stryer, Biochemistry: A Short Course (3rd ed.): a resting human uses about 40 kg of ATP in 24 hours while the body holds about 100 g, so ATP is recycled constantly.
ATP is hydrolysed to ADP and phosphate when it is used, and ATP synthase in mitochondria makes most of it back (standard biochemistry textbooks; Watt et al. 2010, PNAS 107:16823).
description: Your whole body holds only about 100 grams of ATP, yet you use around 40 kilograms of it every day, even resting. Chapter 1 of our book The Tiny Turbine That Powers Your Body. #shorts #biology #science #ATP
sources: Tymoczko, Berg & Stryer, Biochemistry: A Short Course, 3rd ed. (ATP turnover); Watt et al. 2010, PNAS 107:16823 (ATP synthase).

scenes.narration: Even resting, you use about forty kilograms of a molecule called ATP every day.
But your whole body holds only about a hundred grams of it at any moment.
ATP is the energy coin your cells spend. Every muscle pull and every nerve signal is paid in ATP.
When it's spent, it loses a piece and becomes ADP.
So every molecule has to be rebuilt again and again, hundreds of times a day.
The rebuilding happens in your mitochondria, on a machine that spins like a turbine.
You hold only about a hundred grams of ATP, yet you burn through about forty kilograms of it every day.
So what do you think happens to all those turbines when you start to run?
